key_insight: IDiom is an autoregressive protein language model for intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and RL-SAE steers generation by rewarding sparse autoencoder features linked to desired biological functions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a controllable, interpretable design workflow for protein engineering where conventional structure-based methods are ineffective, enabling rapid generation of IDRs with targeted functional properties.
method: Train IDiom on IDiom-DB, a dataset of 54 million predicted IDRs curated from AlphaFold Database.
Use reinforcement learning with sparse autoencoder features (RL-SAE) to explicitly reward activation of selected feature sets.
Generate sequences that preserve natural IDR properties while composing features associated with specific functions.
evidence_signal: Across eight IDR design tasks, RL-SAE sequences activated about 90% of 30 targeted features on average, versus 24% for activation steering, and improved predicted localization and transcriptional activity.
watch_item: Results are based on predicted features and computational evaluations, so experimental validation is still needed before assuming the designed IDRs will behave as intended in vivo.
paper_title: Generative modeling of intrinsically disordered protein regions by reinforcing sparse autoencoder features
